title: Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
content_md: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (also known as Nightmare Eclipse) has released a new Windows zero-day exploit that can let attackers gain SYSTEM privileges. Named SignDrop , it exploits mitigations Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to defend against authentication attacks targeting vulnerabilities in the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver. Naceri added that attacks exploiting CLFS vulnerabilities dropped sharply after the mitigation, but that Microsoft's mitigation itself introduced this new vulnerability. According to Naceri, the flaw is in how CLFS handles creating the authentication file (".cnpf") when it creates a new log file. He said that CLFS enforces access checks correctly at the start, but the logic can be abused if a different, privileged process later opens the log file. He also added that privileged processes such as Windows Defender can be forced to open the files, so the authentication file gets created with SYSTEM privileges, and CLFS creates it with the original file's access permissions. Naceri noted that Microsoft implemented the mitigation properly but that "the logic allows abuse" and said the technique works against any antimalware engine's self-defense (tamper protection), because the file-creation request appears to come from the engine's own legitimate process. "If everything is chained correctly, funnily, this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation of privileges. Everything is done properly by Microsoft
